answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making admission cost real work: every new node first mines a proof-of-work, like cracking a stubborn walnut, and then earns vouches from established peers, building trust the way a reef grows coral layer by layer. A single operator cannot cheaply spawn thousands of clones, because each clone needs fresh compute and time to collect attestations, so the cost of faking many identities starts to spiral upward far faster than any rewards the copies could claim.
